properties.name: A store's identity file is placed beside the store's REAL directory however the path is spelled, the places an older reflow2 used are still read, and a refused open writes nothing
properties.rationale: Fixes the cause in fact:root-cause-a-stores-identity-file-is-placed-by-how-its-path-was-spelled-2026-10-05: a sidecar was located by the path's spelling rather than by the directory it belongs to, and the open's writes were not ordered after its last refusal. Owner's constraint (Anthony, 2026-10-05): "I just want to make sure the changes we implement for vscode don't break it for how it was originally used/designed as an mcp server. My brother likes using as is" — so a store opened by its plain path behaves exactly as before (same two files beside the store, same record), and stores the RELEASED 0.76.0 binary made through a symlink and as `.` are committed as fixtures and pinned to still open, by their old spelling and now by their real path. WHY A COPY, NOT A MOVE: the copy is what makes the real path open; leaving the old file is what keeps an older reflow2 that opens by the same spelling working. NOT DONE, deliberately: the version stamp, client record and usage ledger still follow the spelling (the same class, but none is fatal and moving them changes what an older binary reads); the work machine's own store still needs its id file put back by hand, which the refusal now says how to do. The one behaviour change is loud and needs two identity files naming different designs for one store, which only a reflow2 older than the 2026-08-07 refusal or a hand edit could leave.
properties.subject: system
properties.summary: identity_path now resolves the store's real path (store_real_path: canonicalize, and for a store a first open has not created, the deepest existing ancestor canonicalized with the rest taken lexically), so a new identity file always lands beside the real directory. identity::locate reads, in order: beside the real store; beside the path as typed (a symlink, where 0.79.0 and earlier put it); inside the store (`..id.json` for `.`, `.id.json` for `./`). An identity found only in an older place is used, a copy is written beside the store once the open has succeeded, the old file is never moved or deleted, and the open says so once on stderr and in loop_status (identity_on_open). Two files naming different designs: the one beside the store wins and the other is reported in loop_status `next`. The open now settles identity BEFORE any write: a store with data and no identity file is asked whether it holds the pre-identity design through a READ-ONLY RocksDB open (no info LOG, no lock, no WAL/MANIFEST/OPTIONS rewrite), and a refusal leaves the store and every file beside it byte-identical. The refusal lists every place it looked, the design id(s) the store's own node keys carry (read without writing), the id file that would open it, and where an older reflow2 put the file for a symlink. Identity writes are atomic (temp file + rename). Discover, the registry and the held-read snapshot read identity through the same lookup.
